Continuation Input Response
Acquiring a continuation value for later intervention learning

Private, bounded P3 continuation, 23 October 2026. No old result is changed.
No scientific trajectories were acquired, no application benchmark was added,
and no external persistence was attempted. The accompanying exact calculations
are exposed proof checks, not transfer evidence.

Decision and scope

A learned continuation value can be a reusable input-side procedure: after
a new local intervention, its evaluation replaces an expensive remaining
trajectory when acquiring the intervention's effect on a fixed future reward.
The important interface is a warranted distribution of post-intervention
states. Accuracy on nominal trajectories alone is insufficient.

Here is an obtainable interface. Calibrate the predictor under a randomized
library of executable intervention programs. Their known selection
probabilities provide a simultaneous applicability warrant for later
state-dependent mixtures of those programs. No transition density, unknown
physical density ratio, or universal model membership test is required.

This is a constructive partial-knowledge operation, not a new principle of
intelligence. Its central response algebra is conventional value-function /
Markov-product differentiation. A retaining learner with the same interface
can implement every step. The unresolved practical question is whether a
cheap predictor and its paid domain warrant amortize across enough later
intervention tasks. The result does not establish that they do in a scientific
application.

1. Executable information contract

There is an unknown finite-horizon Markov simulator, with initial sampler mu,
nominal kernels P_t for t=0,...,H-1, and a terminal reward g in [0,1]. Its target
is the simulator's actual numerical law, not an unverified continuous model.
Time, accumulated event flags and all other future-relevant state are included
in a checkpoint. State dimension and transition probabilities need not be
known.

The learner can save a complete checkpoint and generate independent future
nominal continuations from it. Checkpoint copying may be opaque. The learner
also receives permitted metadata phi(x), sufficient to execute a frozen
bounded predictor h_t(phi(x)) and later intervention-selection programs. Opaque
copying alone does not supply such a predictor or make it learnable.

There are m registered, executable one-step intervention kernels R_{t,j},
j=1,...,m. Write R_{t,0}=P_t. An intervention followed by nominal continuation
must actually implement R_{t,j} followed by the same subsequent P kernels.
Persistent modifications must be included in the saved state and in the
calibration domain. A changed physical law cannot silently be treated as an
old continuation.

Training h may use retained data and an ordinary supervised learner. Its
samples, representation, search, failed candidates and numerical work are
charged. Freeze the actual bounded executable predictor before independent
validation; dyadic outputs are convenient. No learnability or rank promise is
assumed here.

For simplicity choose time T uniformly from {0,...,H-1}. Draw X_T by a nominal
prefix, independently choose a label J with known probabilities w_j>0, and
apply R_{T,J} to obtain Y. Save (T,Y) and any metadata required by h. This
defines an obtainable joint reference law

nu(dt,dx,dj,dy) = (1/H) mu_t(dx) w_j R_{t,j}(x,dy).       (1)

Every prefix, intervention, checkpoint and fork is paid. Dyadic label and
policy probabilities give exact finite-bit draws; general rational draws
require their own charged implementation. The analytic weight optimum below
is not silently treated as an executable irrational coin. Equation (1) does
not require knowing any mu_t or R row.

Let

v_t(x) = E[g(X_H) | X_t=x, subsequent dynamics nominal],
e(T,Y) = v_{T+1}(Y) - h_{T+1}(phi(Y)),
S = E_nu e(T,Y)^2.

Independent nominal suffixes from (T,Y) give bounded observations

Z = g(X_H) - h_{T+1}(phi(Y)),       E[Z | T,Y]=e(T,Y).     (2)

Thus the already preserved conditional-replication procedure can return an
upper confidence bound U on S, or INCONCLUSIVE. It does not need to observe
v or identify P. The certificate is an acquisition cost, not a supplied input.
If a poor h fails, training and a fresh valid confirmation attempt cost more.

2. A simultaneous, exact one-intervention certificate

A later policy kappa chooses j>=1 with probabilities kappa_j(t,phi(x)), summing
to one. It may be learned after h is certified. It literally calls the
registered kernels; recognizing an arbitrary new kernel as a member of their
convex hull is not part of the contract.

The scientific experiment makes exactly one intervention: draw uniform T,
run nominally to X_T, choose j using kappa, apply R_{T,j}, then continue
nominally. Denote its expected reward by B_kappa. Let B_0=E_mu v_0 be the
fully nominal reward. A cheap response acquisition instead measures

c_h(kappa) = E[ h_{T+1}(Y_kappa) - h_{T+1}(Y_0) ],       (3)

where Y_kappa and Y_0 are one-step forks from the same nominal context, using
the selected intervention and P_T respectively. No future reward is observed
in (3); h is evaluated on the post-step metadata.

Define a label coefficient on the reference experiment:

A_kappa(t,x,0,y) = -1/w_0,
A_kappa(t,x,j,y) = kappa_j(t,phi(x))/w_j,  j>=1.

Direct substitution in (1) gives

(B_kappa-B_0)-c_h(kappa) = E_nu[A_kappa e].               (4)

Consequently

|(B_kappa-B_0)-c_h(kappa)| <= sqrt(Gamma_kappa S),         (5)

where

Gamma_kappa = E_(T,X_T)[ 1/w_0 + sum_j kappa_j^2/w_j ]
            <= Gamma := 1/w_0 + 1/min_(j>=1) w_j.        (6)

Proof: (4) is an exact signed expectation; Cauchy-Schwarz gives (5), and
sum_j kappa_j^2<=1 gives the uniform upper bound. Neither coefficient needs
a physical density ratio. Gamma_kappa itself can be estimated using nominal
contexts only, with its own confidence cost after kappa is fixed; the
deterministic Gamma needs no such estimation.

On the single acquired event S<=U, inequality (5) holds simultaneously for
every later admissible kappa, including policies chosen after inspecting
the validation data. This is an analytic uniform bias statement. It does not
make an adaptively reused empirical estimate of c_h uniformly accurate.

For example, fix a finite class of Q policies before a fresh evaluation bank.
For each policy, N independent context-and-fork response observations lie in
[-1,1]. Sharing contexts and the nominal fork across policies is allowed.
Hoeffding plus a union bound gives simultaneous sampling error at most eta_p
when

N >= 2 log(2Q/beta)/eta_p^2.                              (7)

The resulting response interval has radius

eta_p + sqrt(Gamma U),                                   (8)

with confidence at least 1-alpha-beta if S<=U has confidence 1-alpha. The same
data can then select a policy from that fixed class. Selecting the largest
empirical c_h loses at most twice (8) against the best true one-intervention
effect in the class. A different policy class needs its own statistical
complexity argument or fresh evaluation; the predictor certificate alone
does not remove that cost.

This gives a concrete subsequent learning operation: one-step intervention
labels can train or select a new policy for a long-horizon reward. Full
system identification and full-domain prediction accuracy are unnecessary.
The newly learned policy is still limited to the registered primitive
interventions, the declared nominal continuation and the fixed reward/horizon.

What the library coverage factor costs

For pure interventions, the largest label factor is

max_j(1/w_0+1/w_j).

Among positive weights its minimum is (1+sqrt(m))^2, attained by
w_0=1/(1+sqrt(m)) and equal w_j=1/[sqrt(m)(1+sqrt(m))]. Indeed,
min_j w_j<=(1-w_0)/m, and

1/w_0 + m/(1-w_0) >= (1+sqrt(m))^2.

Finite-bit programs may choose nearby rational weights and use their exact
larger factor. This is a minimax fact for this label-based single aggregate
L2 warrant, not an information lower bound on every method. Identical or
coupled physical kernels can make (6) very conservative. An equally informed
method may exploit that structure.

The result prevents claiming that a wide intervention library obtains broad
uniform applicability for free: a response bias budget b generally needs
U<=b^2/Gamma. More registered interventions tighten the needed aggregate
calibration unless additional task-specific information is obtained.

3. Repeated perturbations and an exact finite-change limitation

Let R_t^kappa be the selected intervention kernel and apply

P_t^theta = (1-theta) P_t + theta R_t^kappa

at every step. Write J_kappa(theta) for the terminal expected reward. The
finite product rule gives the conventional response identity

J_kappa'(0)
  = sum_t E_mu_t[(R_t^kappa-P_t)v_(t+1)]
  = H(B_kappa-B_0).                                      (9)

Therefore H c_h(kappa) estimates this derivative, with model-bias bound
H sqrt(Gamma U). Derivative acquisition is harder by this H factor for fixed
absolute derivative accuracy; the normalized one-intervention effect in (5)
does not contain that factor.

For every theta in [0,1], without a mixing assumption,

|J_kappa(theta)-J_kappa(0)-theta J_kappa'(0)|
   <= H theta [1-(1-theta)^(H-1)]
   <= H(H-1) theta^2.                                   (10)

Proof: condition on the independent Bernoulli decisions of whether to
intervene at each time. For a fixed subset A of intervention times, let
J_A in [0,1] be the corresponding expected reward. In the remainder, the
coefficient of the empty subset is
(1-theta)^H-1+H theta>=0; each singleton has coefficient
theta[(1-theta)^(H-1)-1]<=0; all larger subsets have positive coefficients.
The positive and negative coefficient masses are equal, and the latter is
H theta[1-(1-theta)^(H-1)]. A [0,1]-valued family J_A yields (10).

This bound is sharp over three-state Markov systems. Let the state count
interventions as 0,1,2-or-more, let P be the identity, let R increment that
count with saturation at 2, and let g be 1 at counts 0 and 2 and 0 at count 1.
Then

J(theta)=1-H theta(1-theta)^(H-1), J(0)=1, J'(0)=-H,

and equality holds in the first bound of (10) for every H and theta. Thus a
certified first response does not by itself warrant arbitrary repeated
intervention effects. The program's exact one-shot operation is the stronger
unqualified finite-change claim.

4. Exact missing-coverage obstruction

There are three states a,z,b, horizon H=2, initial state a and reward 1{b}.
In both worlds nominal dynamics keep a at a and b at b. In world 0, P(z,a)=1;
in world 1, P(z,b)=1. The intervention takes a to z in both worlds. Let
h(a)=h(z)=0 and h(b)=1 at each future time, with h_H=g.

All nominal trajectories, nominal reward observations and nominal prediction
errors are identical in the two worlds; nominal mean-square error is exactly
zero. One-step intervention observations are also identical. Yet a uniformly
timed one-intervention experiment has effect 0 in world 0 and 1/2 in world 1.
The cheap predictor response is zero in both.

Consequently nominal-only experience plus the local intervention output
cannot validate the new response. The missing information is the continuation
from the newly reached state z. With the stated restart contract that
information is obtainable, but it requires a charged future experiment.
With reference weights w_0=w_1=1/2, the actual post-probe squared error is zero
in world 0 and 1/4 in world 1, so the proposed calibration sees the distinction.

If some future intervention has reference weight zero, this example applies
to it. No quantity of repeated samples confined to the old reference support
repairs the absence. Analytically proving membership in a registered mixture,
adding the intervention to the acquisition library, or obtaining a separately
warranted coverage relation is essential.

5. Complete cost and when acquisition really becomes shorter

For every validation checkpoint with sampled time t, preparation costs t+1
kernel calls: t nominal prefix steps and one selected P/R step. Every
independent observation in (2) costs H-t-1 additional nominal transitions,
plus terminal sensing. If checkpoint i uses f_i such observations, the exact
charged transition count is

C_val = sum_i[(t_i+1) + f_i(H-t_i-1)].                    (11)

Add initial sampling, serialization/restoration, independent random streams,
feature extraction, predictor evaluation and certificate arithmetic. If a
conditional-mean certificate uses at most N_cp checkpoints and F conditional
observations, a valid loose step bound is

C_val <= H N_cp + (H-1) F.                              (12)

For a planned squared-error tolerance u, the preserved paired-walk or
conventional Bernstein-envelope methods use
O(u^-1 log(1/alpha) log(1/u)) conditional observations in their stated tolerant
power regime. They return a warranted U<=u or INCONCLUSIVE; the paired-walk
power guarantee requires S<=u/8. These observations are suffix experiments,
potentially O(H) transitions each. For response bias b, plan u=b^2/Gamma.
Calibration can therefore cost
O(H Gamma b^-2 log(1/alpha) log(Gamma/b^2)) transitions, before training and
preparation constants. The lower-tolerance power requirement must also hold;
a valid inconclusive return is not a free certificate.

Matched-accuracy comparison with a strong direct estimator

The direct same-access estimator uses the same nominal contexts, makes one
P fork and one selected R fork, completes each nominal suffix, and returns
the terminal reward difference. It is exactly unbiased for B_kappa-B_0.
It has no finite-difference bias, no transition-density requirement and no
learned domain warrant. It can retain all suffixes, share its nominal reward
across tasks, and use available couplings or variance adaptation.

For a finite class of Q policies, share an IID nominal context bank and the
nominal fork across tasks. Using the elementary bound (7), define

N_d = ceil(2 log(2Q/beta)/eta^2),
N_h = ceil(2 log(2Q/beta)/(eta-b)^2),  b=sqrt(Gamma U)<eta.

Ignoring already separately charged nontransition operations, expected source
work for this explicit pair of implementations is

C_direct = N_d[(H-1)/2 + (Q+1)(H+1)/2],
C_value  = A + N_h[(H-1)/2 + (Q+1)],                     (13)

where A contains all predictor training, search and validation transition
costs. The prefix costs (H-1)/2 per context are present in both expressions;
the nominal fork is shared, so it is Q+1 rather than 2Q. The h procedure also
performs N_h(Q+1) predictor evaluations. These equations compare a declared
distribution-free confidence design, not optimal variances or wall time.

With b=eta/2, approximately N_h=4N_d. The asymptotic incremental source cost
per added policy is then lower only if H>7. Even then total savings require

A < N_d[(H-1)/2+(Q+1)(H+1)/2]
         - N_h[(H-1)/2+(Q+1)],                          (14)

plus an allowance for h computation, copying and storage. Large H alone does
not establish (14). With only one fresh task, the nominal prefix and the
extra precision required by model bias can erase the putative gain. With a
wide primitive library, Gamma grows and may erase amortization again.

The concrete favorable regime is limited: cheap executable h with a
successfully paid small-error warrant; expensive remaining suffixes; a useful
retained or shareable nominal context distribution; and enough changed
intervention-selection tasks within the warranted library to pay (14).
For adaptively proposed arbitrary policies, reserve fresh contexts or pay a
valid policy-class generalization bound. An old empirical context bank is
not automatically a guarantee for every future state-dependent decision rule.

This establishes a conditional reduction in later source work, not superiority
to the best same-information method. The strongest retaining learner can
learn, validate and execute exactly the same h. It can also fit local action
values, retain the full intervention-reward table on its context bank, or use
ordinary approximate policy iteration. Architecture comparison: tie.

6. Primary context and consequences for this branch

The scientific obstruction is substantive: long-horizon event probabilities
are expensive to obtain by direct trajectory observation. Strahan, Finkel,
Dinner and Weare develop short-trajectory Feynman-Kac learning with adaptive
data acquisition, including a 75-dimensional stratospheric-warming model.
That work is a strong existing learner, not an application established for
the present intervention certificate. [1]

Kakade and Langford's conservative policy iteration already combines a
restart distribution, approximate value/advantage information, and mixtures
of policies to improve subsequent decisions. The reusable-procedure idea
cannot be claimed as new on that description. [2] Heidergott and Vazquez-Abad
derive finite-product Markov-kernel sensitivity expressions and unbiased
gradient estimators; (9) is an elementary specialization of this established
response calculus. [3]

The scoped addition preserved here is the explicit, simulator-only
post-intervention validation interface, its known-label coverage constant,
the simultaneous partial-domain error statement, and its complete amortization
conditions. Historical priority for that combination has not been established.
No scientific application, practical advantage, or general intelligence law
has been demonstrated. This direction deserves further work only if a real
intervention library admits a predictive h and the full costs in (14) beat
strong retained value-function / action-value alternatives. Increasing the
number of authored policies would not resolve that question.

7. Exact audit and reproducibility

The inputs were recorded in FROZEN_ALGEBRA_CHECK.json before executing
exact_response_audit.py. The author chose and had theoretical exposure to all
cases. Exact rational matrix arithmetic checked three policies, eighteen
finite-theta bounds, forty-two sharp-remainder identities, and both worlds
of the uncovered-channel obstruction. Every assertion passed on the first
execution. Scientific observations acquired: zero.

The three-policy fixture explicitly calculates v and S only as an audit
oracle for the proof; the learner contract does not receive them. The fixture
does not train h, certify it from data, or demonstrate a useful scientific
error tolerance. It is not a benchmark win. All inputs, outputs and source
hashes are retained in this directory.

Reproduce from the workspace root:

python p3_representation/acquisition_frontier/partial/response_input/exact_response_audit.py
Sources and exposure

[1] Strahan et al., Predicting rare events using neural networks and
short-trajectory data, J. Comput. Phys. 488, 112152 (2023),
https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.01717v2 and
https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jcp.2023.112152.
The primary abstract was read in this bounded task. Governing full-text
sections were previously read by the external worker and are recorded in
../../external/STOPPED_RESIDUAL_NEXT_MECHANISM.md; detailed claims beyond the
abstract are not independently reasserted here.

[2] Kakade and Langford, Approximately Optimal Approximate Reinforcement
Learning, ICML 2002, pp.267-274. Primary paper at
https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~pabbeel/cs287-fa09/readings/KakadeLangford-icml2002.pdf.
The abstract/introductory account was read; the downloaded text layer was
garbled, so this note relies only on the readable abstract-level description
for attribution. No paper-specific finite-horizon theorem is assumed.

[3] Heidergott and Vazquez-Abad, Measure-Valued Differentiation for Markov
Chains, J. Optim. Theory Appl. 136,187-209 (2008),
https://doi.org/10.1007/s10957-007-9297-7.
The primary publisher abstract was read. It directly describes finite-product
derivatives and unbiased estimators; subscription-only proofs were not read.

Internal reusable certificate:
../../root/PAIRED_WALK_RESIDUAL_THEOREM.md and the conventional comparison in
../checkpoint_multiscale_audit/BERNSTEIN_BUDGET_COMPARISON.md. Their stronger
same-access retaining comparison and all earlier failures remain unchanged.

4. Exact missing-coverage obstruction

There are three states a,z,b, horizon H=2, initial state a and reward 1{b}.
In both worlds nominal dynamics keep a at a and b at b. In world 0, P(z,a)=1;
in world 1, P(z,b)=1. The intervention takes a to z in both worlds. Let
h(a)=h(z)=0 and h(b)=1 at each future time, with h_H=g.

All nominal trajectories, nominal reward observations and nominal prediction
errors are identical in the two worlds; nominal mean-square error is exactly
zero. One-step intervention observations are also identical. Yet a uniformly
timed one-intervention experiment has effect 0 in world 0 and 1/2 in world 1.
The cheap predictor response is zero in both.

Consequently nominal-only experience plus the local intervention output
cannot validate the new response. The missing information is the continuation
from the newly reached state z. With the stated restart contract that
information is obtainable, but it requires a charged future experiment.
With reference weights w_0=w_1=1/2, the actual post-probe squared error is zero
in world 0 and 1/4 in world 1, so the proposed calibration sees the distinction.

If some future intervention has reference weight zero, this example applies
to it. No quantity of repeated samples confined to the old reference support
repairs the absence. Analytically proving membership in a registered mixture,
adding the intervention to the acquisition library, or obtaining a separately
warranted coverage relation is essential.

5. Complete cost and when acquisition really becomes shorter

For every validation checkpoint with sampled time t, preparation costs t+1
kernel calls: t nominal prefix steps and one selected P/R step. Every
independent observation in (2) costs H-t-1 additional nominal transitions,
plus terminal sensing. If checkpoint i uses f_i such observations, the exact
charged transition count is

C_val = sum_i[(t_i+1) + f_i(H-t_i-1)]. (11)

Add initial sampling, serialization/restoration, independent random streams,
feature extraction, predictor evaluation and certificate arithmetic. If a
conditional-mean certificate uses at most N_cp checkpoints and F conditional
observations, a valid loose step bound is

C_val <= H N_cp + (H-1) F. (12)

For a planned squared-error tolerance u, the preserved paired-walk or
conventional Bernstein-envelope methods use
O(u^-1 log(1/alpha) log(1/u)) conditional observations in their stated tolerant
power regime. They return a warranted U<=u or INCONCLUSIVE; the paired-walk
power guarantee requires S<=u/8. These observations are suffix experiments,
potentially O(H) transitions each. For response bias b, plan u=b^2/Gamma.
Calibration can therefore cost
O(H Gamma b^-2 log(1/alpha) log(Gamma/b^2)) transitions, before training and
preparation constants. The lower-tolerance power requirement must also hold;
a valid inconclusive return is not a free certificate.

Matched-accuracy comparison with a strong direct estimator

The direct same-access estimator uses the same nominal contexts, makes one
P fork and one selected R fork, completes each nominal suffix, and returns
the terminal reward difference. It is exactly unbiased for B_kappa-B_0.
It has no finite-difference bias, no transition-density requirement and no
learned domain warrant. It can retain all suffixes, share its nominal reward
across tasks, and use available couplings or variance adaptation.

For a finite class of Q policies, share an IID nominal context bank and the
nominal fork across tasks. Using the elementary bound (7), define

N_d = ceil(2 log(2Q/beta)/eta^2), N_h = ceil(2 log(2Q/beta)/(eta-b)^2), b=sqrt(Gamma U)<eta.

Ignoring already separately charged nontransition operations, expected source
work for this explicit pair of implementations is

C_direct = N_d[(H-1)/2 + (Q+1)(H+1)/2], C_value = A + N_h[(H-1)/2 + (Q+1)], (13)

where A contains all predictor training, search and validation transition
costs. The prefix costs (H-1)/2 per context are present in both expressions;
the nominal fork is shared, so it is Q+1 rather than 2Q. The h procedure also
performs N_h(Q+1) predictor evaluations. These equations compare a declared
distribution-free confidence design, not optimal variances or wall time.

With b=eta/2, approximately N_h=4N_d. The asymptotic incremental source cost
per added policy is then lower only if H>7. Even then total savings require

A < N_d[(H-1)/2+(Q+1)(H+1)/2] - N_h[(H-1)/2+(Q+1)], (14)

plus an allowance for h computation, copying and storage. Large H alone does
not establish (14). With only one fresh task, the nominal prefix and the
extra precision required by model bias can erase the putative gain. With a
wide primitive library, Gamma grows and may erase amortization again.

The concrete favorable regime is limited: cheap executable h with a
successfully paid small-error warrant; expensive remaining suffixes; a useful
retained or shareable nominal context distribution; and enough changed
intervention-selection tasks within the warranted library to pay (14).
For adaptively proposed arbitrary policies, reserve fresh contexts or pay a
valid policy-class generalization bound. An old empirical context bank is
not automatically a guarantee for every future state-dependent decision rule.

This establishes a conditional reduction in later source work, not superiority
to the best same-information method. The strongest retaining learner can
learn, validate and execute exactly the same h. It can also fit local action
values, retain the full intervention-reward table on its context bank, or use
ordinary approximate policy iteration. Architecture comparison: tie.

6. Primary context and consequences for this branch

The scientific obstruction is substantive: long-horizon event probabilities
are expensive to obtain by direct trajectory observation. Strahan, Finkel,
Dinner and Weare develop short-trajectory Feynman-Kac learning with adaptive
data acquisition, including a 75-dimensional stratospheric-warming model.
That work is a strong existing learner, not an application established for
the present intervention certificate. [1]

Kakade and Langford's conservative policy iteration already combines a
restart distribution, approximate value/advantage information, and mixtures
of policies to improve subsequent decisions. The reusable-procedure idea
cannot be claimed as new on that description. [2] Heidergott and Vazquez-Abad
derive finite-product Markov-kernel sensitivity expressions and unbiased
gradient estimators; (9) is an elementary specialization of this established
response calculus. [3]

The scoped addition preserved here is the explicit, simulator-only
post-intervention validation interface, its known-label coverage constant,
the simultaneous partial-domain error statement, and its complete amortization
conditions. Historical priority for that combination has not been established.
No scientific application, practical advantage, or general intelligence law
has been demonstrated. This direction deserves further work only if a real
intervention library admits a predictive h and the full costs in (14) beat
strong retained value-function / action-value alternatives. Increasing the
number of authored policies would not resolve that question.
